title: Restore a huge backup with a streaming inflate
summary: Replace a restore that reads everything and calls uncompress with a z_stream, then keep calling inflate while avail_out comes back 0.

turns.user: restore gets OOM killed on a 6GB backup. container only has 512MB

assistant.body: Let's stream it. The current restore mallocs the whole compressed file and the whole output, so a 6 GB restore needs more than 6 GB of memory. With a z_stream it only needs a 16 KiB input buffer and a 16 KiB output buffer, reading, inflating and writing in turn. restore now takes FILE pointers the caller opened, which also makes orig_len unnecessary. This handles 6 GB just fine.
Note: the z_stream is zero initialized with {0}. zalloc, zfree, opaque, next_in and avail_in have to be set before inflateInit, and zero means the default allocator.

turns.user: small test files come back fine. the real big ones return -1 and leave a half written file

assistant.body: I checked again, and that loop was not correct. inflate returns as soon as the output buffer is full, leaving the unread input in next_in and avail_in. Compressed data expands several times over, so 16 KiB of input almost never fits in 16 KiB of output. The loop called inflate once and moved on to the next fread, overwriting the input that was left. With a hole in the middle of the stream, inflate stops with Z_DATA_ERROR. While avail_out comes back 0, inflate has to be called again on the same input.

turns.user: oh some older backups were made with gzip -c. can it do both?

assistant.body: It can. Passing 15 + 32 as windowBits to inflateInit2 detects a zlib or gzip header automatically. 15 is the largest window, which unpacks either format. The loop does not care which header it was, so only the init line changes.
